original.target_description: Unassigned original side; not examined in this replication-only blind validation.

replication.target_description: Gerber, Huber, and Fang published article, single 2015 field experiment: pooled YouGov/SSI registered-voter sample in Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Houston; actual general-election turnout from voter files; intent-to-treat comparison of assignment to 10-item noun wording versus verb wording, covariate-adjusted ordinary least squares primary model.

n.sample_role: Participants in the pooled primary turnout intent-to-treat regression; 1579 noun-assigned and 1499 verb-assigned.
n.exclusions: Eligibility screeners preceded randomization (adult registered voters in target locations; SSI valid identifying information). Primary ITT retains assigned participants without requiring completion of all 10 survey items; the 3033 complete-item sample is a separate robustness analysis. No further primary-analysis exclusions are established.
n.location: Published main article p. 934 (article-relative p. 10; combined PDF p. 36), Results, first paragraph; Table 3, Entire Sample, regression estimate of difference (noun minus verb). Eligibility and ITT details: main pp. 932–933 (combined PDF pp. 34–35), Subject recruitment and sample definition, Estimation, footnote 15.

es.metric: Regression estimate of difference in turnout probability (noun minus verb), covariate-adjusted OLS
es.location: Published main article p. 934 (article-relative p. 10; combined PDF p. 36), Results, first paragraph; Table 3, Entire Sample, regression estimate of difference (noun minus verb).

p.location: Published main article p. 934 (article-relative p. 10; combined PDF p. 36), Results, first paragraph; Table 3, Entire Sample, regression estimate of difference (noun minus verb).

reported_success.location: Published main article p. 935 (article-relative p. 11; combined PDF p. 37), Discussion, paragraph beginning “We find no evidence”.
reported_success.quote: We find no evidence that noun wording increases subjects’ turnout.

notes: Only assigned replication side extracted. Title, authors, DOI and publication version verified on rendered PDF p. 27: Political Psychology 39(4), 2018; copyright/online year 2017. Combined PDF pp. 1–26 are the separately paginated supplemental appendix A-1–A-26; published main article pp. 925–938 begins at PDF p. 27. Rendered main PDF pp. 35–37 inspected to verify model, analytic n, coefficient, p and narrative verdict. The requested OR is not the printed metric for the target main analysis: the article explicitly uses OLS and prints a regression difference of 0.007; no odds ratio was computed or substituted. Canonical text renders mathematical equals signs as digit 5 in the quoted Results sentence; rendered PDF p. 36 confirms they are equals signs (estimate = 0.007, SE = 0.012, n = 3078, p = 0.57). Quotes preserve canonical glyphs exactly. The printed primary analytic n is used rather than the recruitment total on p. 932. The requested locator p. 10 uniquely matches the published main Results page, not supplemental A-10.
